tagline: Down from Hon-Dah to the trout hatchery on the North Fork.
intro: SR 73 leaves Highway 260 at Hondah, by the tribe's Hon-Dah Resort Casino, and heads south into the Fort Apache Indian Reservation, home of the White Mountain Apache, in country covered mostly by pine forest below the Mogollon Rim. The scenic road is eleven miles of it, and ADOT counts the Alchesay and Williams Creek fish hatcheries among its points of interest.
SR 73 was one of Arizona's original state routes of 1927. The hatchery takes its name from Alchesay, a White Mountain Apache chief and Army scout who received the Medal of Honor.

moments.title: Alchesay National Fish Hatchery
moments.text: In a canyon of the White River's North Fork, nine miles north of Whiteriver, trout are raised for the waters of 17 reservations and pueblos, and visitors may fish for the threatened Apache trout.

moments.title: Fort Apache Historic Park
moments.text: South past Whiteriver, the Army post founded in 1870 at the suggestion of White Mountain Apache leaders keeps 27 historic buildings, ruins and its old parade ground as a tribal park.
